summary: This program stores a herd of goats as a list of dictionaries, then uses filter with a lambda to pick out only the goats whose calm level is 7 or higher, and prints them.

lines.text: Opens a list literal that spans several lines, which is allowed in Python because the brackets keep the expression open.
Each goat is a dictionary with a name and a numeric calm level, so related facts about one animal stay bundled together.
filter walks the list and keeps only the items for which the lambda returns True; wrapping it in list() turns the lazy filter object into a real list you can loop over more than once.
The \n at the start prints a blank line first, which separates the heading from anything above it in the terminal.
Loops over the filtered results rather than the original herd, so only the calm goats are reported.
Inside an f-string that uses double quotes, the dictionary keys are written with single quotes so the quoting does not collide.
